title: Dictionaries
description: dict keys, values, and common mapping patterns
theory:
### Dictionaries as the core mapping

`dict` stores key→value pairs with fast lookup. Keys must be hashable (immutable
and comparable predictably). Insertion order is preserved (Python 3.7+ language
guarantee). Use dict comprehensions and unpacking merges (`{**a, **b}` or `a | b`
on 3.9+) for concise joins.

### Patterns that scale

`collections.Counter`, `defaultdict`, and `ChainMap` extend mapping workflows.
Prefer `.get` or membership tests instead of catching `KeyError` when absence is
normal control flow—reserve exceptions for truly exceptional cases.

```python
counts = {c: "aeiou".count(c) for c in "sequoia"}
merged = {"x": 1} | {"y": 2}

from collections import defaultdict

dd = defaultdict(list)
dd["k"].append(1)
```

exercises.title: Create Map
exercises.description: Create a map ages with keys "Alice" (25), "Bob" (30). Print the map.
hints: Use dict literals like {"Alice": 25, "Bob": 30} then print.

exercises.title: Map Lookup
exercises.description: Create map scores = dict{"Math": 95, "Physics": 88}. Look up "Math" and print the score.
hints: scores["Math"] reads the keyed value directly.

exercises.title: Add to Map
exercises.description: Create empty map names = empty dict. Add entries: "1" -> "One", "2" -> "Two". Print map.
hints: Assign bracket keys names["1"] / names["2"] before printing the dict snapshot.

exercises.title: Delete from Map
exercises.description: Create map data = dict{"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}. Delete "b", then print the map.
hints: Remove entries with del data["b"] before displaying what remains.

exercises.title: Check Key Existence
exercises.description: Create map inventory = dict{"apples": 5, "oranges": 3}. Check if "bananas" exists and print exists or not found.
hints: "key in inventory" distinguishes presence from absence.
Choose between exists and not found strings accordingly.
exercises.solution:
inventory = {"apples": 5, "oranges": 3}
print("exists" if "bananas" in inventory else "not found")

exercises.title: Map Length
exercises.description: Create map counts = dict{"one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3}. Print the number of entries using len().
hints: len(counts) returns how many key/value pairs remain.

exercises.title: Iterate Map
exercises.description: Create map grades = dict{"A": 90, "B": 80, "C": 70}. Print each key-value pair.
hints: for key, value in grades.items(): pairs labels with scores.
print(key, value) emits space-separated tuples per line.
